name: Sizing
description: Canonical control, icon, and target dimensions.
rationale: Use a compact 32/40px control system, a 12/16/20px icon system, and a separate 44px interaction target. This aligns well with current productivity-oriented design systems, which commonly organize controls around 32px and 40px heights, use 16px as the standard interface icon size, and distinguish visual component size from the larger hit area required for comfortable interaction. Keeping these dimensions on a 4px-oriented scale also improves alignment with spacing, typography, and component geometry.
guidance: Use the 40px medium control as the default for buttons, inputs, selects, and other standard controls. Use the 32px small control for dense toolbars, tables, filters, and other compact application UI; do not use it merely to fit more content. Keep control widths content-driven unless the component requires a fixed or full width. Use 16px icons for most interface actions and navigation, 12px icons for compact supporting indicators such as chevrons or metadata, and 20px icons when additional prominence or legibility is needed. Interactive elements smaller than 44px should retain or receive an effective hit area of at least 44px where practical, especially for isolated controls and touch-capable interfaces.
notes: Treat visual size and interaction-target size as separate concerns. A 16px icon does not imply a 16px clickable region, and a compact 32px control can use an expanded invisible hit area when surrounding layout permits. Avoid arbitrary intermediate control or icon sizes; prefer the canonical sizes so alignment and density remain predictable. Use larger component dimensions only when a component has a specific hierarchy, accessibility, or touch requirement rather than introducing additional global sizes.
